::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[If document class is equal to something then do not use package](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/46223/if-document-class-is-equal-to-something-then-do-not-use-package), asked by [Atilla Ozgur](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/3976/atilla-ozgur) on TeX Stack Exchange (2012-02-29; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I am trying to create a file which includes common packages and macros I use. It is something like this. 
>
> commonDefinitions.tex
>
> ```latex
>  \interdisplaylinepenalty=2500
>  \usepackage{algorithmic}
>
>  \usepackage{cite} 
>  \usepackage{appendix}
>  ... other packages and macros
> ```
>
> But some packages clash with each other in combinations. For example when I try to use 
>
> ```latex
>  \documentclass[journal]{IEEEtran}
>  \usepackage{appendix}
> ```
>
> It gives error since IEEEtran already created command appendix. 
>
> I would like to get some solution to this problem something like below.
>
> ```latex
> if document class is not IEEEtran 
>    \usepackage{appendix}
> end if
> ```
:::

[I was advised once to test on functionality rather than on class name][1].  The problem is that both `appendix.sty` and `IEEEtran.cls` defines `\appendices`.  So only load the `appendix` package if there isn't already a command `\appendices` defined.  Here is a working example:

```latex
\documentclass{IEEEtran}
\title{Test of conditional use of the appendix package}
\usepackage{lipsum} % just for dummy text
\ifcsname appendices\endcsname
  % do nothing
\else
  \usepackage{appendix}
\fi

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Foo}

\lipsum

\section{Bar}

\lipsum

\appendix

\section{Appendix}

\lipsum

\end{document}
```

`\ifcsame` is available on all e-TeX builds and is documented (along with other ways to check if a command is defined) [here](https://texfaq.org/FAQ-isdef).


  [1]: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/2524614/detect-latex-class-name
